title: A Teenager Discovered a New Planet While Doing a School Project

paragraphs.text: A 17-year-old student from New York made an amazing discovery last week. While working on a school science project with a small telescope, he found a new planet outside our solar system. Scientists at NASA later confirmed his finding. The news quickly spread across the internet, and many people called him a young genius.
paragraphs.translation: 上周，一名来自纽约的17岁学生在学校科学项目中取得了惊人的发现。他用一台小型望远镜发现了一颗太阳系外的新行星。美国宇航局的科学家后来确认了他的发现。这个消息迅速在网上传开，很多人称他为少年天才。

paragraphs.text: The planet is about six times bigger than Earth. It is very far away — more than 1,000 light-years from us. The planet goes around a star that looks a lot like our sun. Scientists say the surface of the planet is extremely hot, over 800 degrees, so there is probably no life there. But the planet's atmosphere is still very interesting to study.
paragraphs.translation: 这颗行星大约是地球的六倍大。它离我们非常远——超过一千光年。这颗行星围绕着一颗看起来很像太阳的恒星运行。科学家说这颗行星的表面极其炎热，超过800度，所以那里可能没有生命。但这颗行星的大气层仍然非常值得研究。

paragraphs.text: The discovery is still very important. It shows that young people can do real science, not just read about it in textbooks. The student, named Jack Chen, spent three months looking at data from his school's small telescope. He said he almost missed the evidence because the signal was very weak. 'You need a lot of patience,' Jack said. 'But when you find something, it feels amazing.'
paragraphs.translation: 这个发现仍然非常重要。它表明年轻人也可以做真正的科学研究，而不仅仅是在课本上读到它。这位名叫Jack Chen的学生花了三个月时间查看学校小型望远镜的数据。他说他差点错过了这个证据，因为信号非常微弱。Jack说："你需要很多耐心，但当你发现什么东西的时候，感觉太棒了。"

paragraphs.text: NASA has invited Jack to visit their space center this summer. He will meet real astronomers and learn more about how to explore the universe. Jack said he plans to study physics in college and hopes to discover more planets in the future. 'I just wanted to finish my school project,' he said with a smile. 'I never thought I would find a whole new world.'
paragraphs.translation: 美国宇航局已邀请Jack今年夏天参观他们的航天中心。他将见到真正的天文学家，并学习更多关于如何探索宇宙的知识。Jack说他计划在大学学习物理学，希望将来能发现更多的行星。他笑着说："我只是想完成学校项目，从没想过会发现一个全新的世界。"

title: Giant Pandas Are No Longer Endangered, but Their Survival Still Needs Help

paragraphs.text: China announced great news for animal lovers around the world last month. The giant panda, one of the most famous animals on the planet, has been moved from 'endangered' to 'vulnerable' on the global species list. This achievement is the result of more than 50 years of hard work by scientists, local communities, and the Chinese government.
paragraphs.translation: 上个月，中国向全世界的动物爱好者宣布了一个好消息。大熊猫——地球上最著名的动物之一——已经从全球物种名单中的"濒危"级别降至"易危"级别。这一成就得益于科学家、当地社区和中国政府50多年的辛勤努力。

paragraphs.text: The key reason for this success was protecting the pandas' natural habitat. Over the past few decades, China has created more than 60 panda nature reserves. These protected areas now cover nearly 2.6 million hectares of bamboo forest. Pandas depend almost completely on bamboo for food — an adult panda eats about 12 to 38 kilograms of bamboo every single day.
paragraphs.translation: 这一成功的关键原因是保护了大熊猫的自然栖息地。在过去的几十年里，中国建立了60多个大熊猫自然保护区。这些保护区的面积现在覆盖了近260万公顷的竹林。大熊猫几乎完全依赖竹子为食——一只成年大熊猫每天要吃大约12到38公斤的竹子。

paragraphs.text: Scientists have also developed new methods to help pandas reproduce in zoos and research centers. Breeding pandas in captivity was once considered extremely difficult, but researchers now understand much more about panda behavior and biology. In 2025 alone, more than 40 panda cubs were born in breeding centers across China.
paragraphs.translation: 科学家们还开发了新方法来帮助大熊猫在动物园和研究中心繁殖。圈养大熊猫的繁殖曾经被认为极其困难，但研究人员现在对大熊猫的行为和生物学有了更多了解。仅在2025年，中国各地的繁殖中心就有超过40只熊猫幼崽出生。

paragraphs.text: However, experts warn that the job is not finished. Climate change could destroy large areas of bamboo in the future. If the bamboo forests disappear, the pandas will lose their main source of food. Scientists estimate that climate change could reduce panda habitat by more than 35% by the end of this century. We need to continue our efforts to protect these beautiful animals and the environment they live in.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，专家们警告说这场战斗还没有结束。气候变化在未来可能会摧毁大面积的竹林。如果竹林消失，大熊猫将失去主要的食物来源。科学家估计，到本世纪末，气候变化可能会使大熊猫的栖息地减少超过35%。我们需要继续努力保护这些美丽的动物以及它们赖以生存的环境。

title: How Esports Became a Billion-Dollar Industry That Rivals Traditional Sports

paragraphs.text: Just ten years ago, most people thought video games were just a fun hobby for teenagers. Today, competitive gaming — known as esports — has grown into a global industry worth more than 1.8 billion dollars. Millions of fans around the world now watch professional gamers compete in huge arenas, and the biggest tournaments offer prize pools larger than many traditional sporting events.
paragraphs.translation: 就在十年前，大多数人还认为电子游戏只是青少年的有趣爱好。如今，竞技游戏——即电子竞技——已经发展成为一个价值超过18亿美元的全球产业。全世界数百万粉丝现在观看职业玩家在大型场馆中比赛，最大赛事的奖金池超过了许多传统体育赛事。

paragraphs.text: The rise of esports has been driven by several key factors. First, internet streaming platforms like Twitch and YouTube Gaming allow anyone to watch live matches for free. Second, game developers like Riot Games and Valve have invested heavily in creating competitive leagues with regular seasons, playoffs, and world championships. Third, major brands such as Nike, Coca-Cola, and Mercedes-Benz now sponsor esports teams and events, bringing serious money into the industry.
paragraphs.translation: 电子竞技的崛起由几个关键因素推动。首先，Twitch和YouTube Gaming等互联网直播平台让任何人都能免费观看现场比赛。其次，拳头游戏和Valve等游戏开发商大力投资创建竞技联赛，设有常规赛季、季后赛和世界锦标赛。第三，耐克、可口可乐和梅赛德斯-奔驰等大品牌现在赞助电子竞技队伍和赛事，为这个行业带来了大量资金。

paragraphs.text: However, becoming a professional esports player is not easy. Top players typically practice for 10 to 14 hours every day, studying game strategy, analyzing opponents, and improving their reaction speed. Many professional teams now employ coaches, nutritionists, and even sports psychologists to help players maintain their physical and mental health. 'People underestimate how much discipline it takes,' said Li Wei, a 19-year-old professional player for a top Chinese team. 'It is not just playing games — it is a real career that requires total dedication.'
paragraphs.translation: 然而，成为职业电竞选手并不容易。顶尖选手通常每天练习10到14个小时，研究游戏策略、分析对手、提高反应速度。许多职业战队现在聘用教练、营养师甚至运动心理学家，帮助选手保持身心健康。19岁的中国顶级战队职业选手李伟说："人们低估了这需要多少自律，这不只是打游戏——这是一份需要全身心投入的真正职业。"

paragraphs.text: China has become one of the biggest markets for esports in the world. The country officially recognized esports as a professional sport in 2019, and many universities now offer degree programs in esports management. In 2025, China's national esports team won three gold medals at the Asian Games, further proving that competitive gaming deserves the same respect as traditional athletics. For millions of young Chinese gamers, esports represents not just entertainment, but a genuine career path and a source of national pride.
paragraphs.translation: 中国已成为全球最大的电子竞技市场之一。该国于2019年正式承认电子竞技为职业体育项目，许多大学现在开设电子竞技管理学位课程。2025年，中国国家电竞队在亚运会上赢得三枚金牌，进一步证明了竞技游戏值得与传统体育同等的尊重。对数百万中国年轻游戏玩家来说，电子竞技不仅代表娱乐，更是一条真正的职业道路和国家自豪感的来源。

title: A 14-Year-Old Diver Won Gold and Made History at the Olympic Games

paragraphs.text: A 14-year-old Chinese diver shocked the world last week by winning a gold medal at the Summer Olympics. She scored a total of 466.20 points in the women's 10-meter platform event, the highest score ever recorded in Olympic history. When the final results appeared on the screen, the audience burst into thunderous applause. Many people compared her performance to a perfect work of art.
paragraphs.translation: 上周，一名14岁的中国跳水选手在夏季奥运会上夺得金牌，震惊了全世界。她在女子10米跳台项目中获得了466.20分的总成绩，这是奥运会历史上记录的最高分。当最终成绩出现在屏幕上时，全场爆发出雷鸣般的掌声。许多人将她的表现比作完美的艺术品。

paragraphs.text: The young athlete started diving when she was only six years old. Her coach said she showed extraordinary talent from the very beginning. 'She has almost perfect technique and incredible mental strength for someone her age,' the coach told reporters. 'During training, she would repeat a single dive hundreds of times until every tiny detail was exactly right.'
paragraphs.translation: 这位年轻的运动员从六岁开始跳水。她的教练说，她从一开始就展现出非凡的天赋。教练告诉记者："在她这个年纪，她有着近乎完美的技术和令人难以置信的心理素质。在训练中，她会把一个跳水动作重复几百次，直到每一个细节都完全正确。"

paragraphs.text: However, her journey to Olympic glory was not simple. Two years ago, she suffered a serious injury during a practice session and could not train for nearly four months. Many people worried that she might never return to her best form. But she refused to quit. 'Lying in bed, all I could think about was getting back to the pool,' she said. 'Diving is not just a sport for me — it is what I truly love.'
paragraphs.translation: 然而，她的奥运荣耀之路并不简单。两年前，她在一次训练中受了重伤，几乎四个月无法训练。许多人担心她可能再也无法恢复到最佳状态。但她拒绝放弃。她说："躺在床上，我满脑子想的都是回到泳池。跳水对我来说不只是一项运动——它是我真正热爱的事情。"

paragraphs.text: Her story has inspired millions of young athletes across China. Many schools now use her experience as an example of how determination and passion can help people overcome any challenge. When asked about her future plans, the young champion smiled and said: 'I want to keep improving and show the world what Chinese athletes can achieve.' Her victory proves that age is never an obstacle when you have enough dedication and courage.
paragraphs.translation: 她的故事激励了中国数百万年轻运动员。许多学校现在用她的经历作为例子，说明决心和热情如何帮助人们克服任何挑战。当被问及未来计划时，这位年轻冠军微笑着说："我想继续进步，向世界展示中国运动员可以取得的成就。"她的胜利证明，当你有足够的奉献和勇气时，年龄从来不是障碍。

title: Scientists Discover That Crows Can Solve Problems as Well as a Seven-Year-Old Child

paragraphs.text: Crows may be much smarter than you think. A new study published in the journal Nature shows that these birds can solve complex puzzles at a level similar to a human child aged seven. The research team from Cambridge University designed a series of experiments to test how crows think and make decisions. The results surprised even the scientists themselves.
paragraphs.translation: 乌鸦可能比你想象的要聪明得多。发表在《自然》杂志上的一项新研究表明，这些鸟类解决复杂谜题的能力相当于七岁的人类儿童。剑桥大学的研究团队设计了一系列实验来测试乌鸦如何思考和在决策。结果连科学家自己也感到惊讶。

paragraphs.text: In one experiment, the crows were given a task that required multiple steps to get food. They had to drop stones into a narrow tube to raise the water level, then use a stick to reach the floating treat. Most crows figured out the solution within three minutes. Some even learned to choose heavier stones first, as if they understood basic principles of physics. The scientists described this as 'remarkable evidence of logical thinking in a non-human species.'
paragraphs.translation: 在一项实验中，乌鸦被给予一个需要多个步骤才能获得食物的任务。它们必须将石头投入狭窄的管中来提高水位，然后用一根棍子够到漂浮的食物。大多数乌鸦在三分钟内就找到了解法。有些乌鸦甚至学会了先选择更重的石头，仿佛它们理解了基本的物理原理。科学家将此描述为"非人类物种逻辑思维的显著证据"。

paragraphs.text: Crows also demonstrated impressive memory abilities. During the study, they could recognize individual human faces and remember whether a particular person had treated them kindly or not. A year after the initial encounters, the crows still showed different reactions to 'friendly' and 'unfriendly' researchers. This long-term memory is extremely rare in the animal kingdom outside of mammals.
paragraphs.translation: 乌鸦还展示了令人印象深刻的记忆能力。在研究过程中，它们能识别人类个体的面孔，并记住某个人是对它们友善还是不友善。在初次接触一年后，乌鸦对"友好"和"不友好"的研究人员仍然表现出不同的反应。这种长期记忆在哺乳动物以外的动物界极为罕见。

paragraphs.text: The discovery could change how we think about animal intelligence. For a long time, scientists believed that only primates like chimpanzees and gorillas had advanced problem-solving skills. This research suggests that intelligence may evolve in many different forms across the animal world. The lead scientist Professor James Morrison noted: 'We should not assume that a small bird brain cannot achieve great things. Nature constantly challenges our assumptions about intelligence.'
paragraphs.translation: 这一发现可能改变我们对动物智力的看法。长期以来，科学家认为只有黑猩猩和大猩猩等灵长类动物才具有高级的问题解决能力。这项研究表明，智力可能在动物界以许多不同形式演化。首席科学家James Morrison教授指出："我们不应假设一个小的鸟脑不能取得伟大的成就。大自然不断挑战我们对智力的假设。"

title: A 12-Year-Old Girl Invented a Device That Cleans Ocean Water Using Solar Power

paragraphs.text: A 12-year-old girl from Fujian province has won an international science award for inventing a small device that can clean polluted ocean water using only solar energy. Her invention, which she calls the 'Ocean Broom,' uses a combination of natural filters and sunlight to remove harmful chemicals and tiny plastic pieces from seawater. The device can clean about 100 liters of water in a single day.
paragraphs.translation: 一名来自福建省的12岁女孩因发明了一种仅使用太阳能就能净化污染海水的小型装置而赢得了国际科学奖。她的发明被称为'海洋扫帚'，利用天然过滤器和阳光的组合来去除海水中的有害化学物质和微小塑料碎片。这个装置一天可以净化大约100升水。

paragraphs.text: The young inventor said she got the idea after seeing plastic waste on a beach near her home. 'I felt very sad when I saw dead fish and birds covered in plastic,' she explained. 'I wanted to create something that could help solve this problem, even if only in a small way.' She spent nearly eight months designing and testing different versions of her device before finding one that worked effectively.
paragraphs.translation: 这位年轻发明家说，她是在家附近的沙滩上看到塑料垃圾后产生这个想法的。她解释说：'当我看到死去的鱼和鸟被塑料覆盖时，我感到非常难过。我想创造一些可以帮助解决这个问题的东西，哪怕只是很小的帮助。'她花了将近八个月的时间设计和测试不同版本的装置，才找到了一个有效的方案。

paragraphs.text: Scientists and environmental experts have praised her work as both creative and practical. One judge at the competition described her invention as 'a perfect example of how young minds can tackle global challenges with simple, elegant solutions.' Several major companies have already expressed interest in helping her develop the device for wider commercial use. Her school has also announced plans to build a small laboratory where she and other students can continue their research.
paragraphs.translation: 科学家和环保专家称赞她的工作既有创意又实用。比赛的一位评委将她的发明描述为'年轻头脑如何用简单而优雅的解决方案应对全球挑战的完美范例'。几家大公司已经表示有兴趣帮助她开发这个装置用于更广泛的商业用途。她的学校也宣布计划建造一个小型实验室，让她和其他学生可以继续他们的研究。

paragraphs.text: Despite all the attention, the girl remains humble and focused on her goal. 'I don't think of myself as a genius,' she said. 'I just saw a problem and tried to solve it. Anyone can do that if they care enough.' She hopes her story will inspire other young people, especially girls, to pursue their interest in science and technology. 'The ocean belongs to everyone,' she added. 'And everyone can help protect it.'
paragraphs.translation: 尽管备受关注，这个女孩仍然保持谦虚，专注于她的目标。她说：'我不认为自己是天才，我只是看到了一个问题并尝试解决它。只要足够关心，任何人都可以做到。'她希望自己的故事能激励其他年轻人，特别是女孩，去追求她们对科学和技术的兴趣。她补充道：'海洋属于每个人，每个人都可以帮助保护它。'

title: A Blind Pianist from Shanghai Performed at Carnegie Hall and Moved the Audience to Tears

paragraphs.text: Last weekend, a 19-year-old blind pianist from Shanghai gave a performance at Carnegie Hall in New York that moved the entire audience to tears. Chen Wei lost his eyesight when he was only three years old due to a rare disease, but he discovered his passion for music at the age of five when he first touched a piano keyboard. 'I cannot see the keys, but I can feel them,' he said. 'Music became my window to the world.'
paragraphs.translation: 上周末，一位来自上海的19岁盲人钢琴家在纽约卡内基音乐厅的演出让全场观众感动落泪。陈伟在三岁时因一种罕见疾病失去了视力，但他在五岁时第一次触摸钢琴键盘时发现了对音乐的热情。他说：'我看不见琴键，但我能感受到它们。音乐成了我通往世界的窗口。'

paragraphs.text: Learning to play the piano without sight required extraordinary determination. Chen had to memorize every single note of every piece by listening to recordings repeatedly. His teacher said that while most students might practice a difficult section dozens of times, Chen would practice it hundreds of times until every note was perfect. 'His memory is remarkable, but it is his spirit that truly sets him apart,' the teacher commented. 'He never complains. He just keeps working.'
paragraphs.translation: 在没有视力的情况下学习弹钢琴需要非凡的决心。陈伟必须通过反复听录音来记住每首曲子的每一个音符。他的老师说，大多数学生可能把困难段落练习几十遍，而陈伟会练习几百遍，直到每个音符都完美。老师评论道：'他的记忆力很出色，但真正让他与众不同的是他的精神。他从不抱怨，只是不断努力。'

paragraphs.text: At the Carnegie Hall concert, Chen performed works by Chopin, Beethoven, and a modern Chinese composer. The highlight of the evening was his performance of Chopin's 'Fantaisie-Impromptu,' a piece known for its technical difficulty and emotional depth. Several audience members were seen wiping away tears during the performance. When he finished, the hall erupted in a standing ovation that lasted for more than five minutes.
paragraphs.translation: 在卡内基音乐厅的音乐会上，陈伟演奏了肖邦、贝多芬和一位中国现代作曲家的作品。当晚的亮点是他演奏的肖邦《幻想即兴曲》，这是一首以技术难度和情感深度著称的曲子。观众中有人被看到在演出期间擦拭眼泪。当他结束时，音乐厅爆发出持续超过五分钟的起立鼓掌。

paragraphs.text: Chen's dream is to establish a music school for children with disabilities, where they can learn to express themselves through music regardless of their physical limitations. 'Being blind does not mean you cannot have a vision,' he said with a gentle smile. 'Music taught me that limitations exist only in our minds. If I can help even one child discover that truth, then everything I have gone through will be worth it.' Several music organizations have already offered to support his project.
paragraphs.translation: 陈伟的梦想是为残疾儿童建立一所音乐学校，让他们无论身体有何限制都能通过音乐表达自己。他带着温和的微笑说：'失明并不意味着你不能有远见。音乐教会我，限制只存在于我们的思想中。如果我能帮助哪怕一个孩子发现这个真理，那么我所经历的一切都是值得的。'几个音乐组织已经表示愿意支持他的项目。

title: A 16-Year-Old Boy Built a Free Coding School for Children in Rural Villages

paragraphs.text: When 16-year-old Li Wei visited his grandmother in a small mountain village in Guizhou province, he noticed that children there had no computers at school. While his school in Beijing had a full computer lab and coding classes, these rural students had never even seen a programming interface. This experience inspired him to start a project that would change the lives of hundreds of children.
paragraphs.translation: 当16岁的李伟去贵州省一个小山村看望祖母时，他注意到那里的孩子在学校没有电脑。他在北京的学校有完整的计算机实验室和编程课，而这些农村学生甚至从未见过编程界面。这次经历激励他发起了一个项目，改变了数百名孩子的生活。

paragraphs.text: Li used his savings and raised money online to buy twenty used laptops. He then spent his weekends and holidays traveling to three rural villages, setting up small classrooms in community centers. There, he taught children aged 8 to 14 basic programming concepts using simple visual tools. In less than a year, over 200 children attended his free coding workshops.
paragraphs.translation: 李伟用自己的积蓄并在网上筹集资金，购买了二十台二手笔记本电脑。然后他利用周末和假期前往三个乡村，在社区中心设立了小型教室。在那里，他用简单的可视化工具教8到14岁的孩子基础编程概念。不到一年，超过200名孩子参加了他的免费编程工作坊。

paragraphs.text: The results were remarkable. Several students created simple mobile apps to help their parents with farming tasks, such as tracking weather patterns and calculating crop yields. One 12-year-old girl designed a mini-program that reminded elderly villagers to take their medicine on time. 'These children are not less smart than city kids,' Li said firmly. 'They just need an opportunity to discover what they can do.'
paragraphs.translation: 结果非常显著。几名学生创建了简单的手机应用来帮助父母做农活，比如追踪天气模式和计算作物产量。一个12岁的女孩设计了一个小程序，提醒村里的老人按时服药。李伟坚定地说：'这些孩子并不比城里孩子笨，他们只是需要一个机会去发现自己能做什么。'

paragraphs.text: Li's project has now attracted attention from technology companies and education organizations. A major Chinese tech firm donated 50 additional laptops and promised to help train volunteer teachers. Li plans to expand the program to ten more villages next year. 'Coding is not just about getting a job at a tech company,' he explained. 'It teaches you how to think logically and solve problems. Every child deserves that skill, no matter where they live.'
paragraphs.translation: 李伟的项目现在已经吸引了科技公司和教育机构的关注。一家中国大型科技公司捐赠了50台额外的笔记本电脑，并承诺帮助培训志愿者教师。李伟计划明年将项目扩展到另外十个村庄。他解释说：'编程不只是为了在科技公司找到工作，它教你如何有逻辑地思考和解决问题。每个孩子都应该拥有这种能力，无论他们住在哪里。'

title: Chinese Astronaut Taught a Physics Lesson from the Space Station to Millions of Students

paragraphs.text: Last Tuesday, millions of students across China gathered in their classrooms to watch a very special physics lesson — it was being taught live from the Tiangong space station, orbiting 400 kilometers above the Earth. Astronaut Wang Yufei, a former physics teacher who joined the space program six years ago, demonstrated how everyday physical phenomena behave completely differently in microgravity.
paragraphs.translation: 上周二，中国各地数百万学生聚集在教室里观看一堂非常特别的物理课——这堂课是在距离地球400公里的天宫空间站上直播的。宇航员王宇飞六年前加入航天项目，曾是一名物理老师，他展示了日常物理现象在微重力环境下的完全不同的表现。

paragraphs.text: During the 45-minute lesson, Wang showed several fascinating experiments. She squeezed a wet towel and instead of dripping, the water formed a floating bubble around the towel. She spun a toy gyroscope that kept its orientation stable without any support. She also demonstrated how a pendulum behaves in space — instead of swinging back and forth, it moved in circular patterns that would be impossible on Earth. Students reacted with gasps of wonder and enthusiastic applause.
paragraphs.translation: 在这45分钟的课程中，王宇航员展示了几个令人着迷的实验。她挤了一条湿毛巾，水没有滴下来，而是在毛巾周围形成了一个漂浮的水球。她旋转了一个玩具陀螺，陀螺在没有任何支撑的情况下保持了稳定的方向。她还展示了钟摆在太空中的行为——它不像在地球上那样来回摆动，而是以在地球上不可能的圆形轨迹运动。学生们发出惊叹和热烈的掌声。

paragraphs.text: Between experiments, Wang answered questions sent by students from around the country. One primary school student asked if you could cry in space. Wang smiled and explained that tears would not fall but form a floating ball of water around your eyes, which made the students laugh. A high school student asked about the challenges of sleeping in space, and Wang demonstrated how astronauts strap themselves into sleeping bags attached to the wall so they do not float away during the night.
paragraphs.translation: 在实验间隙，王宇航员回答了全国学生发来的问题。一个小学生问在太空中能不能哭。王宇航员笑着解释说，眼泪不会掉下来，而是会在眼睛周围形成一个漂浮的水球，这让同学们笑了。一个高中生问在太空中睡觉有什么挑战，王宇航员演示了宇航员如何把自己绑在固定在墙上的睡袋里，以免在夜间飘走。

paragraphs.text: The space lesson was part of China's ongoing effort to inspire the next generation of scientists and engineers. Over 60 million students watched the live broadcast, and the hashtag related to the event was viewed more than 500 million times on social media. 'When I was their age, I looked up at the stars and dreamed of touching them,' Wang said at the end. 'Today, you are looking at the stars from a classroom that floats among them. Imagine what you will achieve when you grow up.'
paragraphs.translation: 这堂太空课是中国持续激励下一代科学家和工程师的努力的一部分。超过6000万学生观看了直播，相关话题在社交媒体上的浏览量超过5亿次。王宇航员在结束时说：'我在你们这个年纪的时候，抬头看星星，梦想着触摸它们。今天，你们从一颗漂浮在星空中的教室里仰望星空。想象一下，当你们长大后会取得什么样的成就。'

title: A Teenage Girl Won the Google Science Fair with a Low-Cost Water Purifier That Uses Sunlight

paragraphs.text: A 15-year-old girl from India has won the top prize at this year's Google Science Fair for creating a water purification device that costs less than five dollars to build. The device, which she named 'SunPure,' uses sunlight and a few simple materials to turn dirty water into clean drinking water in just two hours. Her invention could help millions of people in developing countries who lack access to clean water.
paragraphs.translation: 一名15岁的印度女孩因发明了一款造价不到5美元的水净化装置而赢得了今年谷歌科学博览会的大奖。她将这个装置命名为'SunPure'，它利用阳光和几种简单材料在短短两小时内将脏水变成干净的饮用水。她的发明可以帮助发展中国家数百万缺乏清洁饮用水的人。

paragraphs.text: The idea came to her when she visited her grandmother in a rural village where people had to walk three kilometers every day to collect water from a river. The river water was often contaminated and caused many health problems. She started experimenting with different materials in her family's small kitchen, using old plastic bottles, sand, charcoal, and a special type of glass that focuses sunlight to kill harmful bacteria.
paragraphs.translation: 这个想法是在她去一个农村看望祖母时产生的，那里的人们每天要走三公里去河里取水。河水经常被污染，导致许多健康问题。她开始在家中的小厨房里用不同的材料进行实验，使用旧塑料瓶、沙子、木炭和一种能聚焦阳光以杀死有害细菌的特殊玻璃。

paragraphs.text: What makes her design special is that it does not need electricity, batteries, or expensive filters. It works entirely on solar power and natural materials that can be found almost anywhere. Independent tests showed that the SunPure device can remove more than 99% of harmful bacteria from contaminated water. A panel of judges described her work as 'remarkable in its simplicity and potential for global impact.'
paragraphs.translation: 她的设计特别之处在于不需要电、电池或昂贵的过滤器。它完全依靠太阳能和几乎在任何地方都能找到的天然材料。独立测试表明，SunPure装置可以去除污水中超过99%的有害细菌。评审团称她的工作是'以其简洁性和潜在的全球影响而引人注目'。

paragraphs.text: Now she plans to use the prize money to build 1,000 SunPure units and distribute them to villages in need across India. Several international organizations have also offered to help her scale up the production. 'I did not want to just read about water problems in a textbook and feel sad about them,' she said during her acceptance speech. 'I wanted to do something real that could actually change people's lives. Every child deserves clean water, and every child can be a scientist.'
paragraphs.translation: 现在，她计划用奖金制造1000个SunPure装置，并将它们分发给印度各地有需要的村庄。几个国际组织也表示愿意帮助她扩大生产规模。她在获奖演讲中说：'我不想只是在课本上读到水问题然后感到难过，我想做一些真正能改变人们生活的实事。每个孩子都应该拥有干净的水，每个孩子都可以成为科学家。'

title: Learning Two Languages Can Delay Brain Aging by Up to Five Years, New Study Finds

paragraphs.text: A major new study published in the journal 'Neurology' has found that people who speak two or more languages regularly may experience slower brain aging and a delay in the onset of memory problems by up to five years. Researchers followed more than 1,200 people over a period of twenty years, testing their memory, attention, and problem-solving abilities at regular intervals.
paragraphs.translation: 发表在《神经学》期刊上的一项重大新研究发现，经常使用两种或以上语言的人大脑衰老速度更慢，记忆问题的出现可能推迟多达五年。研究人员在二十年间跟踪了1200多人，定期测试他们的记忆力、注意力和解决问题的能力。

paragraphs.text: The study found that bilingual individuals performed significantly better on cognitive tests, especially in areas of attention control and task switching. The researchers believe that constantly managing two languages — choosing the right word in the right language and suppressing the other — acts like a daily workout for the brain. This mental exercise strengthens the brain's executive function, which is responsible for planning, focusing, and making decisions.
paragraphs.translation: 研究发现，双语者在认知测试中表现显著更好，特别是在注意力控制和任务切换方面。研究人员认为，不断管理两种语言——选择正确的语言中的正确词汇并抑制另一种语言——就像每天对大脑进行锻炼。这种心理锻炼加强了大脑的执行功能，该功能负责计划、专注和决策。

paragraphs.text: Interestingly, the protective effect was found regardless of when the second language was learned. People who learned a second language in childhood benefited, but so did those who started learning in their forties or fifties. The key factor seemed to be regular use of both languages, not the age at which learning began. This is encouraging news for adults who might think it is too late to start learning a new language.
paragraphs.translation: 有趣的是，无论第二语言是什么时候学的，都发现了这种保护效应。童年时期学习第二语言的人受益，但四五十岁才开始学习的人也受益。关键因素似乎是经常使用两种语言，而不是开始学习的年龄。这对那些可能认为现在开始学习新语言为时已晚的成年人来说是个令人鼓舞的消息。

paragraphs.text: The lead researcher noted that language learning combines several brain-healthy activities into one: memorization, pattern recognition, sound processing, and social interaction. 'It is never too late to start,' she emphasized. 'Even modest progress in a new language can provide meaningful cognitive benefits. You do not need to become perfectly fluent — the learning process itself is what protects your brain.'
paragraphs.translation: 首席研究员指出，语言学习将几种有益大脑健康的活动合为一体：记忆、模式识别、声音处理和社交互动。她强调：'开始学习永远不会太晚。即使是新语言中的适度进步也能提供有意义的认知益处。你不需要变得完全流利——学习过程本身就是在保护你的大脑。'
